starting-off.speaker: Trufitus
starting-off.text: Greetings Bwana! I am Trufitus Shakaya of the Tai Bwo Wannai village.

options.text: What does Bwana mean?

steps.player: What does Bwana mean?

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: It means friend, and friends come in peace. I assume that you come in peace?

options.text: Yes, of course I do.

steps.player: Yes, of course I do.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: Well, that is good news, as I may have a proposition for you.

options.text: A proposition eh? Sounds interesting!

steps.player: A proposition eh? Sounds interesting!

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: I hoped you would think so. My people are afraid to stay in the village.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: They have returned to the jungle and I need to commune with the gods

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: to see what fate befalls us. You can help me by collecting some herbs that I need.

options.text: Me? How can I help?

steps.player: Me? How can I help?

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: I need to make a special brew! A potion that helps me to commune with the gods. For this potion, I need very special herbs, that are only found in the deep jungle.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: I can only guide you so far as the herbs are not easy to find. With some luck, you will find each herb in turn and bring to me. I will give you details of where to find the next herb.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: In return for this great favour I will give you training in Herblore.

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: It sounds like just the challenge for me. And it would make a nice break from killing things!

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: That is excellent Bwana! The first herb that you need to gather is called

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: Snake Weed.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: It grows near the vines in an area to the south west where

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: the ground turns soft and the water kisses your feet.

options.text: No.

steps.player: Hmmm, sounds difficult, I don't know if I am ready for the challenge.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: Very well then Bwana, maybe you will return to me invigorated and ready to take up the challenge one day?

options.text: I am very sorry, but I don't have time for that.

steps.player: I am very sorry, but I don't have any time for that.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: Very well then, may your journeys bring you much joy.

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: Maybe you will pass this way again and you then take up my proposal?

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: But for now, fare thee well.

options.text: I am sorry, but I am very busy.

options.text: What does a warrior like me know about peace?

steps.player: What does a warrior like me know about peace?

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: When you grow weary of violence and seek a more enlightened path, please pay me a visit

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: as I may have a proposition for you. Now I need to attend to the plight of my people. Please excuse me...

options.text: Tai Bwo Wannai? What does that mean?

steps.player: Tai Bwo Wannai? What does that mean?

steps.speaker: Trufitus
steps.text: It means 'small clearing in the jungle' but it is now the name of our village.

options.text: It's a nice village, where is everyone?

steps.player: It's a nice village, where is everyone?
